idea-plugin.name: Test-Only Declaration Detector
idea-plugin.description:
Reports production Java declarations whose every caller lives in a test source root — production API kept alive only by the tests that assert on it. Such a declaration inflates the public surface, blocks refactoring, and still counts as covered in coverage reports.

Methods, fields and whole classes are reported. When a class turns out to exist only for the tests, it is reported once as a class rather than once per member, so the finding that matters — delete the file — is not buried under its own methods.

Each finding offers a quick fix that annotates the declaration as test-facing (@TestOnly, either @VisibleForTesting), which both silences this inspection and switches on the built-in Test-only usage in production code so production can no longer call it. Only annotations that resolve on the module's classpath are offered.

Why not just use Unused declaration?

IntelliJ can already compute this, via Unused declaration → Entry points → "When entry points are in test sources, mark callees as: unused". But that option works by stripping entry-point status from everything in a test source root, so your @Test methods are reported as unused too, with the identical "never used" message. The distinction is computed and then discarded. It is also a profile-wide setting shared with the on-the-fly unused-symbol inspection, so enabling it changes the daily editor experience.

This plugin reports the same finding as its own category, with its own severity and suppression id, leaving Unused declaration untouched.

What is excluded

  • Declarations with no callers at all — that is plain dead code, and Unused declaration's job.
  • Framework entry points, resolved through the platform's own registered entry points and your Settings | Editor | Inspections | Entry points configuration — so Spring @Bean, @KafkaListener, @Scheduled and @EventListener methods, JPA no-arg constructors and Jackson accessors are left alone.
  • Constructors, main, record accessors, and methods overriding library declarations.
  • Enum constants and record components, whose only source reference can legitimately be the test that names them while production reaches them through valueOf, a deserializer or a column mapping.
  • Nested, local and anonymous classes. Only top-level classes are reported, because a reference from the outer class is internal to the file but external to the nested one, and the plugin will not guess which reading you meant.
  • Declarations carrying an annotation from an editable list, seeded with @TestOnly, both @VisibleForTesting variants, and generated-code markers (@Generated, @AvroGenerated). Add your own team's conventions, or remove entries to report annotated declarations anyway.

Each finding is confirmed against the index before it is reported, so a reference from Spring XML, SpEL, a .properties file or javadoc suppresses it.

How to run it

  • Enable Declaration used only from test code in Settings | Editor | Inspections — it is off by default. Class and field reporting can be switched off there separately, leaving methods only.
  • Run Analyze | Inspect Code with test sources included in the scope. Without them, a test-only declaration is indistinguishable from a fully dead one, and the inspection refuses to guess.
  • This is a global inspection: it runs only via Inspect Code and will never highlight as you type.

Source, documentation and a worked example of every case: GitHub. MIT licensed.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.2
  • Renamed the plugin to Test-Only Declaration Detector, since it no longer reports only methods. The plugin id is unchanged, so this arrives as an ordinary update.
0.3.1
  • Reports fields and whole classes used only from test code, not just methods. A class that exists only for the tests is reported once, and its own methods and fields are not reported underneath it.
  • A class counts as used only when something outside it refers to it or to anything it declares — a static factory returning its own type no longer keeps it alive. Only top-level classes are considered.
  • New quick fix: annotate the declaration as test-facing. Offered only for annotations that resolve on the module's classpath and whose @Target permits that kind of declaration, so the fix can never leave the file uncompilable.
  • Class and field reporting can each be switched off in the inspection settings.
  • An annotation on any enclosing class now suppresses reporting, not only on the immediately containing one.
  • Renamed to Declaration used only from test code. The suppression id and profile key are unchanged, so existing settings carry over.
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Reports production Java methods whose every caller lives in a test source root.
  • Excludes framework entry points, constructors, main, record accessors and methods overriding library declarations.
  • Confirms each finding against the index, so references from Spring XML, SpEL, properties files and javadoc suppress the report.
  • Editable list of annotations that suppress reporting, on the method or its class. Seeded with @TestOnly and both @VisibleForTesting variants, plus generated-code markers (@Generated, @AvroGenerated).
